steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's eligibility criteria—typically a bachelor's degree plus years of direct project leadership, or equivalent alternatives. Verify your qualifications before enrolling to ensure you'll meet application requirements.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course. Attend all 35 required contact hours of formal education on a schedule that fits your work commitments. Our active certified practitioners guide you through the PMBOK® Guide and real-world project scenarios relevant to your career.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, submit your official PMI application with proof of experience, education, and training hours. Pay the examination fee directly to PMI. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your application before scheduling your exam date.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor support—to strengthen your readiness. Schedule your computer-based PMP exam at an authorized testing center. On exam day, demonstrate your mastery of project-management knowledge and earn your credential.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: PMP certification remains valid for three years. Maintain your status by earning professional development units (PDUs) through approved training, volunteer work, and continuing education. Plan your PDU activities throughout the renewal cycle to keep your credential active and stay current in the field.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.
